header:
Is 0% utilization
really the best score?

lines.text: Myth: 0% credit utilization gets you the highest score.
lines.say: Myth: zero percent credit utilization gets you the highest score.

lines.text: Utilization is your reported card balances divided by your limits.
lines.say: Utilization is your reported card balances divided by your limits.

lines.text: myFICO says amounts owed make up about 30% of a FICO Score.
lines.say: myFICO says amounts owed make up about thirty percent of a FICO Score.

lines.text: The twist: myFICO says all cards at $0 can score slightly lower than a small balance, because it can look unused.
lines.say: The twist: myFICO says all cards at zero dollars can score slightly lower than a small balance, because it can look unused.

lines.text: Our math: $150 of a $5,000 limit is 3%. Paid in full, interest is $0.
lines.say: Our math: a hundred fifty dollars of a five thousand dollar limit is three percent. Paid in full, interest is zero dollars.

lines.text: Experian's 2026 data: people with 800+ scores average about 7% utilization.
lines.say: Experian's twenty twenty-six data: people with eight hundred plus scores average about seven percent utilization.

lines.text: For scale, FICO's US average each April: 716 in 2021, a record 718 in 2023, 714 in 2026.
lines.say: For scale, FICO's US average each April: seven sixteen in twenty twenty-one, a record seven eighteen in twenty twenty-three, seven fourteen in twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: So 0% versus low single digits is a tiny gap, and you never need to pay interest.

post.title: Does 0% credit utilization give you the best score?
post.ig:
Myth: 0% credit utilization gets you the highest score.
myFICO says amounts owed make up about 30% of a FICO Score.
myFICO also says every card reporting $0 can score slightly lower than a small reported balance, because $0 can look like no active use.
Our example: $150 on a $5,000 limit is 3% utilization, and paid in full it costs $0 in interest.
People with 800+ FICO Scores average about 7% utilization (Experian, 2026 data). FICO's US average was 714 in April 2026.
The gap between 0% and a low single-digit percent is tiny, and you never need to carry a balance or pay interest.
Sources: myFICO, FICO, Experian.
